purpose: Shared Nostr engine, independent ESP32, Pi, P4 and custom-board signer releases, plus a generic Board/SDK.

status_semantics.ready: No predecessor task is required; reconcile scope and current source before starting.
status_semantics.planned: Predecessors or physical resources are still required.

definition_of_done: Acceptance met on exact candidate commit/artifacts.
Independent review closed for final candidate.
Evidence includes commands/procedures, environment, result and hashes.
Affected integration gates pass after integration.
Documentation and task state agree with source and measurements.
authorization: Maintainer authorizes repository reorganization, archival, publication and local engineering. Reuse this authorization. No specific purchase, fabrication order, production-secret operation or irreversible provisioning is authorized by this plan.

deferred_tracks.track: Additional board models inside supported families
deferred_tracks.entry: An exact new model earns its own physical acceptance and named maintenance owner.
Generic Board SDK and non-Nostr example first; each full application needs protocol, interoperability and security qualification.
Separate measured need, isolation architecture and independent review; ordinary SDK libraries offer no such boundary.

tasks.title: Make the measured baseline reproducible
acceptance: Fresh isolated checkout installs pinned Python, Node/package manager and Rust toolchains with one documented bootstrap.
Resolve sibling/nested layout explicitly; classify stale API generation and integration launcher noise without weakening behavioral checks.
Run relevant software suites and full integration; record skipped live/physical gates and exact input commits.

tasks.title: Define the retained portfolio and per-profile threat models
acceptance: Adopt or revise the four signer profiles and independent developer platform; smartcards leave active scope without losing history.
For each profile define user flows, custody, active channels, boot integrity, trusted UI, physical attacker assumptions and recovery; do not impose a one-dimensional security ranking.
Connected daily-use profiles include NIP-44; initial QR profiles define manual scope, resource/time limits and explicit unsupported capabilities.
Every required guarantee maps to an acceptance gate and real evidence; unavailable hardware properties are not replaced with booleans or silently waived.

tasks.title: Define compatibility and adoption test plans by profile
acceptance: Choose initial client/version candidates and record source-backed protocol support and known gaps; this is test planning rather than completion of every profile integration.
Define separate connected, QR and Board-developer evidence requirements and success measures; actual client timing/interactions/pilots belong to the corresponding implementation/release tasks.
Prepare opt-in research scripts; participant recruitment and identification of an independent Board developer are performed by the profile that needs them, not a universal prerequisite.
No release waits for observations or a participant from an unrelated profile.

tasks.title: Close Bridge identity and bounded-input security gaps
acceptance: Using public fixture keys, reproduce the baseline NIP-46 session-manager acceptance of a changed user signing key and of a foreign signed transport author delivered by an adapter; distinguish this conditional handler gap from exploitability of the default adapter. Pin companion source 13414320537d0208fc3ef8e43bd0723c98c1d5e0 and retain negative regression tests.
Pin authenticated expected signer transport author in the manager itself.
Resolve and bind user identity separately from transport identity; reject unauthorized identity changes and mixed-session/replay responses.
Preserve legal transport/user key separation and verify existing clients and cancellation/error flows.

Reproduce SerialLineStreamPort retaining 20,000 queued bytes from 10,000 short lines with maxBufferedBytes=4; enforce total bytes and request count, backpressure, terminal-error behavior and cleanup, not only per-line limits.

tasks.title: Constrain secret ownership and cryptographic implementation
acceptance: Remove secret-bearing Debug and unnecessary Clone/public secret access; test exposed formatting behavior using public fixture material.
Define lifetimes, copies, zeroization boundaries and internal-memory allocation; do not claim compiler-proof physical erasure from ownership alone.
Qualify maintained crypto/zeroization implementations against exact embedded targets and independent vectors before replacing local primitives.

tasks.title: Make authorization bind exactly one canonical operation
acceptance: Derive identity and canonical event bytes inside the trusted device boundary.
Bind preview, selected identity, full operation and one-use approval; reject mutation, replay, cancellation races and unreviewed metadata.
Bound resource use and handle long/hostile Unicode content without misleading truncation.
An independently computed event ID and signature verifier agree for positive and adversarial vectors.

tasks.title: Specify custom-board SE-assisted custody and owner lifecycle
acceptance: Compare candidate SE architectures against exact APIs and advisory applicability; prove the security contribution of each chip.
Specify every stored object, authenticated ciphertext, host-binding secret, KDF context, pairing key and firmware-signing root.
Cover PIN creation/change/exhaustion, brownout, rollback, recovery, destructive reset and update ownership; model persistent-state transitions.
Preserve NIP-06 compatibility without treating currently unrecommended derivation as the default; prove expected-public-key recovery.
Independent cryptographic review rejects unsupported non-exportability or dual-SE independence claims.
Distinguish developer, owner-secured and product-qualified states; validate MCU and SE erasure/re-enrollment and irreversible-state limits when replacing firmware.

tasks.title: Build the versioned component and manual review register
acceptance: For every candidate record exact part/package/silicon, official document ID/revision/date/URL/hash and relevant errata.
Triage viable alternatives; read and sign off all sections affecting the selected design, with per-pin and requirement citations.
Identify unavailable/restricted documentation and unsupported features before freezing a part.
No full-manual-review claim is made from a link inventory.

tasks.title: Compare bounded MCU feasibility on development hardware
acceptance: Run comparable USB/display/physical-input/crypto and SE API probes on identified boards.
Prove secure boot and recoverable signed-update feasibility after provisioning on sacrificial samples.
Measure resource/pin/power envelope and document toolchain gaps; do not build two full product ports.
Select one host from requirements and measurements; defer complete lifecycle qualification to V02/H08.

tasks.title: Resolve power, display, battery and mechanical envelope
acceptance: Obtain exact panel/connector drawings and validate pinout/contact orientation against actual samples.
Calculate state-based worst-case power, thermal, USB entitlement, charging and full usable cell-range behavior.
Define battery chemistry/protection/temperature, reverse/backfeed behavior and absent-battery operation.
Choose one mechanical reference with readable review screens and accessible test points.

tasks.title: Qualify stable KiCad and a pinned MCP adapter
acceptance: Pin KiCad 10.0.7 and adapter revision after checking current support; begin with read-only operations.
On disposable projects verify supported mutations, undo/rollback, disconnect/crash recovery, layer/coordinate/flip correctness and save/reopen.
Use native-project CLI ERC/DRC and hash-linked exports; distinguish stable PCB IPC from development-only schematic/headless features.
Promote only demonstrated operations; retain one writer per CAD project and independently reviewed source-generation fallback.

tasks.title: Inventory reuse and consumers for the five-repository mapping
acceptance: Classify modules by required behavior and targeted review; retain independent Python/vector oracles.
Inventory released packages, external consumers, tags, issues, licenses and references before deprecating boundaries.
Confirm or revise the proposed five-repository topology with explicit release-boundary reasons.
Separate generic board support/API from Nostr semantics; preserve active Pi/P4 paths; plan smartcard archival and explicit retirement.

tasks.title: Rehearse software consolidation without losing history
acceptance: Import in an isolated repository, preserving provenance and mapping old commits/tags/paths.
Preserve distinct host/embedded target toolchains and build workspaces where needed.
Compare imported trees and run equivalent acceptance; eliminate fixture duplication with one authoritative contract artifact.
Prepare redirect notices and external Nostr interoperability plan; do not archive or publish source repositories without applicable authorization.

Validate only the migrated existing components and topology: ESP32 signer/Pi/P4 code has no custom-board dependency. Do not require unimplemented SDK code or empty-scaffold proof; actual standalone SDK/application independence is accepted in B02/B03.

tasks.title: Install minimal agent coordination and evidence controls
acceptance: Convert the accepted operating model into concise repository instructions with one task-state authority.
Each task records scope, input/candidate commits, worktree ownership, acceptance and independently reviewed evidence.
Use Astra xhigh for requested hardware/security agents, isolated editing worktrees and one CAD writer.
Validate task dependencies and generated views; demonstrate resume from a fresh session without relying on chat memory.
Autonomy preserves existing authorization and respects concrete irreversible-action boundaries without repetitive confirmations.
Track readiness and release evidence separately for all active profiles; no global gate on an unrelated product.

tasks.title: Deliver connected ESP32 signer on a commercial board without SE
acceptance: A real client request reaches trusted display; physical approval returns a valid BIP-340 signature for the exact event and identity.
Host never receives the identity secret; transport and device pairing credentials have explicit lifecycles.
Reject/cancel/replay/substitution/malformed/disconnect cases pass on hardware.
Use public test identities and record actual flashable build, memory map and board version.

tasks.title: Qualify complete custom custody on the selected host
acceptance: Execute complete PIN/custody/backup/restore lifecycle with expected-public-key checks.
Inject power loss at every persistent-state transition; prove safe recovery and no PIN-attempt rollback.
Test unsigned/rollback image rejection, interrupted updates, debug/lifecycle state and post-provisioning recovery.
Verify RNG behavior, secret memory placement and wipe limits on the actual target; independently review remaining exposure.

tasks.title: Complete hardware-backed NIP-07 and NIP-46 serving
acceptance: Implement actual serving direction and tested local browser path on named client/OS versions.
Device authorization authenticates client/session provenance; untrusted origin labels never become authority.
Handle availability, reconnect, account selection, revocation and error states with understandable UX.

tasks.title: Complete connected-profile NIP-44 user-message operations
acceptance: Distinguish relay RPC transport encryption from user-message key operations.
Pass official vectors and named client message flows, including applicable NIP-17/59 semantics.
Define device-enforced permissions and leakage boundaries; do not expose stable conversation keys by convenience.
Document supported payload bounds as product limits rather than protocol maxima.

tasks.title: Freeze the first board architecture
acceptance: Select one exact MCU/SE/panel/power architecture with resolved advisory and documentation requirements.
Keep security buses private; prove isolation and mode transitions for maker interfaces, including power-off/backfeed.
Freeze pin/resource/mechanical budgets and manufacturing provisioning/test requirements.
No unresolved blocker is relabeled as an accepted compromise.

tasks.title: Capture and review the complete schematic
acceptance: Populate real connected circuitry and all required support components.
Validate every symbol/footprint against exact package drawings and each pin against the manual ledger.
ERC plus semantic netlist assertions cover intended power, protection, boot, USB, SE, display and expansion states.
Independent reviewer closes electrical findings before layout freeze.

tasks.title: Route and qualify layout/mechanical/manufacturing constraints
acceptance: Route the real netlist with justified stackup, return paths, decoupling, thermal and USB constraints.
Check enclosure/panel/cable fit and assembly/test access with exact part geometry.
DRC and independent geometry/render/netlist review identify and resolve all violations and justified exceptions.

tasks.title: Prepare the reviewable EVT manufacturing package
acceptance: Generate hash-linked outputs from the reviewed native project and independently inspect manufacturing exports.
Confirm parts availability, assembly process, stackup and fabricator rules; prepare cost/lead-time quote assumptions.
Include bring-up/test procedure, provisioning boundaries and small-lot quantities.
Obtain any missing authorization for the concrete order before manufacturing submission.

tasks.title: Measure first articles and correct the design
acceptance: Execute current-limited bring-up; measure rails/ramp/ripple/transients/current/temperature and protection behavior.
Validate USB, display/input, SE, battery handoff, power-off and interrupted-update recovery on identified assemblies.
Reproduce generic SDK, provisioning, update/recovery and electrical tests on custom boards; record faults and necessary revision.
No simulator result substitutes for an assembly measurement.

tasks.title: Validate the corrected product assembly
acceptance: Build corrected samples if EVT requires changes and repeat affected measurements.
Validate thermal/mechanical/ESD/EMC and battery/product obligations for intended distribution with qualified expertise.
Demonstrate reproducible assembly test and defined pass/fail limits; every measured result names the exact revision.

tasks.title: Close custom Board signer pilot security admission gates
acceptance: Independent security review covers exact pilot software/hardware and applicable physical attacks.
Close all blocking findings; vendor mitigations must meet the accepted guarantees.
Prove backup restoration and firmware authenticity; record explicit real-identity admission or restrict pilot to test identities.

tasks.title: Run the custom Board signer pilot and maker reproduction
acceptance: Run opt-in four-week pilot on admitted identity class and named compatible clients.
Measure onboarding, recurring use, recovery, prompt understanding, support effort and unexplained signatures.
Use proposed 8/10 unaided onboarding and 7/10 weekly retention as hypotheses; all recovery drills restore expected identities and no unexplained signing/key loss is tolerated.
Have an independent maker reproduce the build and a developer integrate the SDK; feed findings into code and requirements.

tasks.title: Qualify custom Board signer production artifacts and provisioning
acceptance: Build actual flashable binaries twice independently; publish source/protocol/board/component/bootloader compatibility manifest.
Rehearse signing-key protection, provisioning ceremony, replacement/recovery and production testing with authorized operators.
Close independent security review for final candidate and any pilot/production changes.
Measure total cost, test yield and support obligations before proposing production quantity or price.

tasks.title: Publish the qualified custom Board signer release and maintain it
acceptance: Publish only authorized reviewed artifacts and exact supported compatibility/security claims.
Provide reproducible build, source/board files, onboarding/recovery and vulnerability-reporting instructions.
Define advisory monitoring, component substitution review and update/support ownership for released units.

tasks.title: Add bounded persistent automation only after device enforcement
acceptance: Review and bind full permission semantics, not merely policy IDs.
Enforce durable counters/revocation and explicit trusted-time/reset model in the device.
Test adversarial host counters, clock rollback and power loss; keep this optional feature outside first-release critical path.

tasks.title: Define per-profile capabilities and real readiness evidence
acceptance: Replace universal target-readiness booleans with requirements for the claimed profile; represent supported/configured/verified/unavailable/unknown distinctly.
No-SE is explicit; missing required SE fails closed. Unsupported methods and custody modes never trigger silent downgrades.
Bridge routes by versioned methods/algorithms/limits and transport; a device claim alone is not proof of security state.
Keep public compatibility contracts and independent vectors common while allowing distinct timing and custody.

tasks.title: Implement the portable Nostr signing engine
acceptance: Implement canonical signing and verify every output under the selected identity using qualified libraries.
Prove one-use consent and exact-review binding with negative tests; preserve independent Python/vector verification.
Compile for selected embedded and Linux targets without board-specific Nostr semantics or mandatory SE dependencies.
Define bounded secret ownership across complete operations; avoid repeatedly copying keys across language/process adapters.
Reject duplicate JSON members, trailing bytes, invalid Unicode and Nostr kind outside 0..65535; keep an independent NIP-01 oracle rather than only cross-language parity.
Replace eager full-page storage where measured memory warrants it; report actual target stack/peak RAM, worst-case parse time and QR buffering. Host size_of results are not target measurements.

tasks.title: Qualify one accessible ESP32 board without SE
acceptance: Identify exact SoC revision, memory, USB, screen/input and hardware connections.
Demonstrate direct display/physical confirmation and boot/update feasibility without borrowing custom-board SE guarantees.
Define volatile demonstration and persistent product modes; list applicable silicon/security limitations.

tasks.title: Qualify ESP32 custody and lifecycle without SE
acceptance: Qualify encrypted persistent custody on the exact MCU before promising daily persistent use; volatile mode is separately named.
Exercise reset/power-cut, unlock attempts, host rollback, unsigned/old images, debug lock and interrupted updates.
Document physical extraction/PIN-enforcement limits honestly; no SE-based claims or borrowed custom Board signer acceptance.
Prove expected-public-key restore and trusted review on actual hardware.

tasks.title: Qualify and release ESP32 signer independently
acceptance: Apply every release_gate_template condition to ESP32 signer and close exact-profile findings.
Run connected-client onboarding, messaging and recovery pilot after independent admission; measure actual artifact reproducibility.
Publish only the tested no-SE profile with applicable authorization; custom hardware readiness is not a dependency.

tasks.title: Define shared offline custody and transport requirements
acceptance: Define optical input/output limits, separate seed import/export, power/update states and permitted data channels.
Define how exact Pi and P4 hardware records prove radio absence/isolation, boot properties and no secret persistence.
Keep hardware feasibility and release status independent between Pi and P4; neither target must pass to work on the other.

tasks.title: Implement Bridge QR request and response workflows
acceptance: Preserve identity/request binding and output verification across manual optical round trips.
Enforce frame/byte/time bounds, reject mixed/replayed requests and separate seed import/export from signing output.
Test actual client deadlines and repeated scans; never extend scope with cached blanket approval or exported identity keys.
Expose unsupported DM/automation capabilities accurately and plan any future compound operation separately.

tasks.title: Deliver Offline Pi with the shared engine
acceptance: Use the shared Rust engine for product signing semantics; preserve Python as independent oracle and reuse useful adapters during migration.
Choose and measure the minimal driver/FFI boundary; any retained UI/input code remains in the trusted computing base.
On the actual kit scan, import a public test identity, review, approve/reject, sign, return QR and verify independently.
Prove session-only custody and no secret writes through logs, swap, dumps or image tooling; preserve a working path until parity passes.

tasks.title: Deliver Offline P4 with the shared engine
acceptance: Build and flash exact P4 target with the selected camera/runtime adapter; share core semantics with ESP32 signer and Pi.
Exercise complete QR request/review/approval/signature cycle, malformed optical input and cancellation on hardware.
Qualify secret placement, no persistent secrets, actual communication modes and authenticated update/recovery.
No claim that P4-family support establishes a particular camera or radio-free board.

tasks.title: Qualify and release Offline Pi independently
acceptance: Apply every release_gate_template condition to this exact offline profile; no connected NIP-44 or custom-PCB prerequisite.
Close independent firmware/image, optical-input/output, boot, physical-substitution, volatile-custody and recovery findings applicable to stated guarantees.
Run optical usability/recovery and independent maker reproduction after profile admission; publish exact limitations and supported kit.
Keep this release independent of the other vault and custom-board production.

tasks.title: Qualify and release Offline P4 independently
acceptance: Apply every release_gate_template condition to this exact offline profile; no connected NIP-44 or custom-PCB prerequisite.
Close independent firmware/image, optical-input/output, boot, physical-substitution, volatile-custody and recovery findings applicable to stated guarantees.
Run optical usability/recovery and independent maker reproduction after profile admission; publish exact limitations and supported kit.
Keep this release independent of the other vault and custom-board production.

tasks.title: Define and extract the Nostr-independent Board SDK
acceptance: Board SDK exposes buses/power/entropy/key handles/algorithms/storage/display/input/lifecycle without Nostr schemas or policy.
Start with libraries in one trusted firmware image; document absence of inter-application security isolation.
Pin electrical contracts from hardware and design version compatibility without circular or sibling-path dependencies.
Development, owner-secured and product-qualified states have explicit transition limits and secret-reset requirements.
required_evidence: standalone build scaffold only when used

tasks.title: Implement Board support and standalone non-Nostr proof
acceptance: Bring up chosen components on evaluation/reference hardware using maintained upstream drivers where appropriate.
Run an independently buildable non-Nostr example that exercises consent and a supported crypto/key operation without importing nsealr.
Keep demonstration protocols labelled as examples; P256/Ed25519 primitives are not claims of complete SSH/FIDO products.
Document custody location, unsupported operations and developer/provisioned recovery behavior.

tasks.title: Integrate and requalify the custom Board signer on the actual custom PCB
acceptance: Repeat Nostr custody, one-use consent, PIN, backup and boot/update/power-cut tests on identified custom assemblies.
Bind actual SDK, bootloader, component, board revision and application in the evidence manifest.
Generic SDK/board acceptance does not substitute for custom Board signer application/security acceptance.

tasks.title: Qualify the generic Board and SDK developer release
acceptance: Apply relevant release_gate_template conditions to the platform without claiming application-level Nostr/FIDO/wallet assurance.
Independent developer builds the non-Nostr example without nsealr and reproduces board bring-up and allowed firmware ownership transitions.
Publish exact schematic/BOM/SDK/bootloader compatibility, production test evidence and lifecycle limitations.
Close independent findings for generic security services before advertising their guarantees; no custom Board signer/client-pilot dependency.

tasks.title: Qualify the exact Pi kit and image feasibility
acceptance: Identify exact Pi model, camera, panel/input and boot-media path; inspect radio and USB hardware.
Prove camera-to-decoder-to-display feasibility and inspect image integrity, swap/logs/dumps and physical substitution risks.
Record target build/toolchain support and whether existing Python adapters can be retained with the shared engine.

tasks.title: Qualify the exact P4 camera and offline hardware feasibility
acceptance: Identify exact silicon, camera, panel and any companion radio; measure or inspect permitted channels.
Prove camera-to-decoder-to-display operation and memory envelope before implementing the complete vault.
Compare supported Rust driver path with a narrow maintained vendor-framework adapter if needed; retain one shared signing engine.

excluded_from_active_roadmap.disposition: Retire smartcard research after verified preservation and a public notice. Keep its repository/history public; no active real-card product is claimed.

release_gate_template: Exact profile, supported hardware, firmware/SDK/bootloader configuration and declared capabilities are pinned.
Profile-specific custody, transport, boot, physical-attacker and recovery guarantees have measured evidence; unavailable properties are never fabricated as configured or verified.
Independent review closes all applicable blocking findings on the candidate; early engineering uses disposable public identities and formal pilot/real identity admission requires these gates.
Pilot/recovery and independent reproduction meet profile-specific acceptance; security is not waived by satisfaction scores.
Actual release artifacts reproduce, are signed as applicable and have accurate installation/recovery/security documentation.
Publication/order/provisioning actions occur only within applicable authorization; each profile can ship without an unrelated profile passing.
sequencing_note: The connected Bridge integration C01 is first proven on the accessible device V01 and reused by the custom Signer path. This is an implementation sequence, not a claim that the custom-board custody design or generic SDK intrinsically depends on a commercial no-SE board. Pi, P4 and accessible releases do not wait for custom fabrication; Board SDK does not wait for the Nostr app.
